mainText: This is Dose of Good for Saturday, November 28. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Black and Indigenous students are a majority at Brazil's federal universities for the first time. According to the higher-education census, Black, mixed-race and Indigenous students make up 50.1% of federal university enrolment, about 659,000 people, up from 22.5% in 2013. Brazil also reached a record 10.6 million university students. Second: Volunteers build rope bridges for sloths in Costa Rica. Since sloths can't jump between trees, a foundation has installed about 410 rope bridges over roads and buildings. Cameras have logged more than 22,000 wildlife crossings, not only by sloths. Third: Ukrainian mental-health workers complete trauma training in Australia. Eight Ukrainians, including psychiatrists and social workers, completed trauma training on scholarships covering travel and living costs. A local resident raised A$22,000 in a raffle for first-aid kits they will take home. Fourth: Low-cost cameras track Brazil's dry ecosystems more precisely. Researchers validated in Brazil and Angola a method using cheap automatic cameras that continuously record when plants leaf out and shed. In the Caatinga, cameras caught the landscape greening right after a single rainfall. Fifth: New algorithm finds in minutes a star that eluded huge searches. Weizmann Institute scientists created a method that found a pulsar spinning more than 260 times a second using little computing power, after an earlier search failed despite the equivalent of 600 years of processing. The method is already finding more pulsars. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
